name: awesome-musicdsp
desc: A curated list of my favourite music DSP and audio programming resources

resources.name: Audio Plug-in Dev Skills
resources.desc: Claude Code marketplace for audio plugin development skills.
resources.section: New - Agentic AI coding tools for audio programmers

resources.name: iPlug2
resources.desc: Originally created by Cockos, iPlug is an awesome plug-in framework. For a long time, I was maintaining a fork of iPlug1, but over the last few years Alex Harker and I have reworked it into something new, with the imaginitive name: iPlug2. It's a massive improvement on the original version, adding support for GPU accelerated vector graphics, resizable high DPI UIs, iOS, WebViews, AUv3 and compiling to WebAudio/WASM, amongst many other things. iPlug2's syntax is super simple, for example, creating a parameter or a control in the UI is only a single line of C++ code.

resources.name: JUCE
resources.desc: JUCE is an undeniably awesome C++ application/plug-in framework with audio roots. It boasts a vast amount of functionality for the development of music software, including support for almost all plug-in formats and platforms. JUCE is used widely in the music technology industry and it has excellent documentation, code standards, features and support. The JUCE team organise the Audio Developer's Conference (ADC) which is one of the best conferences to attend if you like audio programming. What's more all the videos from all the ADCs so far are available on youtube.

resources.name: AudioKit
resources.desc: AudioKit uses the Swift programming language. It's a high level DSP and UI toolkit for audio things. If you want to make apps for Apple's devices this is a great option, although if you want to do more low level, custom DSP, you will still have to do some C/C++.

resources.name: ASPiK
resources.desc: This is a framework from Will Pirkle, used in his books, which is based on the VST3 SDK and it's AU/AAX wrappers, along with VST GUI and its runtime UI editor. It includes a project creator and a lot of extra "nuts and bolts" code for plug-in development.

resources.name: DPF
resources.desc: Distrho Plug-in Framework is a nice C++ plug-in framework by falkTX, supporting lots of Linux formats.

resources.name: Jamba
resources.desc: A new framework built on top of the VST3SDK & VSTGUI, with some useful extra widgets and good CMake support

resources.name: DPlug
resources.desc: A plug-in framework using the D programming language, that has had a huge amount of work over many years. I haven't tried it, but I've decided to include it here in solidarity with the authors. As a fellow open-source framework developer, it's nice if people know about your work.

resources.name: Steinberg VST3 SDK
resources.desc: The Steinberg VST3 SDK has been around for a long time, but recent versions start to add a lot of great features such as really good CMake support, Lots of documentation, and a nice template project. Since Steinberg include wrappers for VST2, AUv2, AUv3 and AAX it is somewhat like a plug-in framework.

resources.name: CPLUG
resources.desc: A smart new plug-in abstraction in C that targets VST3, AUv2, CLAP and Standalone formats on desktop. It's very new but a nice clean and minimal way to target multiple formats producing tiny binaries. Also includes hot reloading capabilities for the standalone targets.

resources.name: iPlug2OOS
resources.desc: Continuing the theme of self-promotion, here is the latest and greatest iPlug2 template project, set up with CI/CD, installer scripts, github workspaces etc.

resources.name: pamplejuce
resources.desc: An excellent template for JUCE projects.

resources.name: wolfsound - audio-plugin-template
resources.desc: Jan Wilczek has made another excellent JUCE template

resources.name: JUCECmakeRepoPrototype
resources.desc: Eyal Amir also has one which looks good!

resources.name: Brad Howes AUv3 Template
resources.desc: A template for iOS/macOS AUv3 projects

resources.name: VSTGUI
resources.desc: VSTGUI is Steinberg's cross-platform UI framework for audio plug-ins. It is released under a BSD licence, it's an impressive piece of work and many plug-in developers use it for their products.

resources.name: Elements
resources.desc: A very promising UI framework for audio software using modern C++.

resources.name: PUGL
resources.desc: A cross platform GLFW-like solution that lets plug-in developers use OpenGL for their UIs

resources.name: Gamma
resources.desc: Gamma is a very awesome C++ DSP library by Lance Putnam. The beauty of Gamma is the conciseness of the implementation of certain techniques. How about this for a concise STFT example.

resources.name: Q
resources.desc: A very nice looking modern C++ DSP library with concise examples

resources.name: HIIR
resources.desc: HIIR is a seriously cool oversampling library by Laurent de Soras. Oversampling is something we often need in audio DSP, and this library handles it elegantly - providing a variety of classes for low latency IIR half band filtering (including SIMD optimizations). Originally this had a LGPL licence but now it's available under the WTFPL - my favourite licence.

resources.name: HOALibrary
resources.desc: A flexible DSP library for high order ambisonics (HOA) - a spatial audio platform that is becoming more and more relevant thanks to VR (GPL Licence).

resources.name: HISSTools Library
resources.desc: a nice BSD licensed library by Alex Harker, including FFT abstractions and multi-channel convolution, amongst other things

resources.name: Mach1 Spatial SDK
resources.desc: Vector based multichannel & spatial audio APIs for customizing multichannel or spatial audio pipelines & tools and agnostically playback any spatial, surround soundfields.

resources.name: Spatial Audio Framework
resources.desc: Another excellent library for ambisonics and other spatial audio related processing

resources.name: MadronaLib
resources.desc: Randy Jones' DSP library, which is awesome because it is all designed for SIMD processing.

resources.name: WDL
resources.desc: WDL is Cockos' library of reusable C++ code, that is used to make the DAW Reaper, amongst other things. It includes open source implementations of many useful things such as resampling and convolution, although there is next to no documentation and the code is difficult to understand. For more info about the various parts of WDL (which can be used independently), check the Cockos site

resources.name: DaisySP
resources.desc: A MIT licensed DSP library written for the Daisy platform, but also useable elsewhere. I like it because it includes some nice ports of Emilie Gillet's mutable instruments code.

resources.name: SignalSmithDSP
resources.desc: A really nice looking DSP library, along with a really nice blog/website with a collection of nice articles, e.g. How to write a reverb, see also a video presentation

resources.name: librosa.cpp
resources.desc: Librosa is a widely used Python library for MIR tasks. With a little help from my agents, i've systematically ported it to a C++ library with WASM and Swift Package to boot.

resources.name: essentia
resources.desc: Essentia is a huge collection of MIR algorithms that you can use to extract high and low level features from audio. AGPL3 license. Somewhat painful to build cross-platform.

resources.name: audioflux
resources.desc: AudioFlux is a new-kid-on the block and some what similar but looks designed for deep learning, it looks very promising and has a liberal (MIT) license.

resources.name: FAUST
resources.desc: FAUST is a powerful functional DSL for audio DSP with many options for quickly compiling to different “architectures” including audio plug-ins and embedded devices. FAUST is not interpreted like programming languages such as Puredata/Max/Supercollider/javascript, it is "transpiled" to C++ and various other programming languages or bytecode formats such as Web Assembly (WASM). This functionality is suited to rapid prototyping but can also produce robust and performant binaries. Whilst the rapid prototyping possibilities of FAUST are appealing to me, what I like most about it is the extensive library of high quality DSP, particularly for physical modelling synthesis and the way in which you can compose algorithms using the concise syntax. FAUST includes a JIT compiler "libfaust" based on LLVM, which I integrated into a JUCE module. I've used it to make a physical model of the Indian Tambura.

resources.name: Cmajor
resources.desc: Is an exciting new DSL created by Jules Storer and Cesare Ferrari, which also uses the LLVM compiler technology. It has a JIT compiler for a fast workflow and can spit out C++ and WASM and ready-to-go JUCE projects. Cmajor is an imperative language much more similar to C/C++/Javascript than FAUST. It has several advantages, for example multi-rate processing and in my opinion it is more suited for code that mixes event-handling with DSP, where as FAUST is good for discreet blocks of DSP processing. Since FAUST can output Cmajor code via faust2cmajor, you can use them together.

resources.name: Filter Playground
resources.desc: A nice blog post and web audio tool demonstrating IIR filters

resources.name: MicroModeler Filter Design Tool
resources.desc: An excellent web based filter design tool

resources.name: DSPFilters
resources.desc: Vinno Falco made this excellent MIT licensed IIR filter library. Here is a fork to work with the latest JUCE. See also iir1, which seems a further developed and improved version.

resources.name: RBJ Cookbook
resources.desc: HTML version of Robert Bristow-Johnson's EQ cookbook

resources.name: Cytomic Technical Papers
resources.desc: Andy Simper's technical papers, which include code examples and theory for modern approaches to filter design

resources.name: Vadim Zavalishin - The Art of VA Filter Design
resources.desc: Very math-heavy text on those modern approachs

resources.name: Will Pirkle
resources.desc: Will Pirkle has written two books that will be invaluable the aspiring audio plug-in developer - "Designing Audio Effect Plug-Ins in C++" and "Designing Software Synthesizer Plug-Ins in C++". The books contain detailed information about important audio DSP, including modern virtual analogue techniques, and sample code for complete sythesizers that sound good. My only criticism is that a large part of the books relates to a bespoke plugin framework and providing information for multiple formats, AU, VST3 can be a bit overwhelming, and clutters the content. Nevertheless I highly recommend these books. For more info see here

resources.name: Dodge and Jerse - Computer Music: Synthesis, Composition and Performance, 2nd Edition
resources.desc: This is my absolute favourite book to recommend to students studying computer music/audio synthesis. I find the book does not date like some other computer music texts. The block diagrams are charming and the techniques are discussed very well.

resources.name: Udo Zölzer (Ed) - DAFX: Digital Audio Effects
resources.desc: This is a great book on audio DSP, written by a variety of domain experts, and it includes Matlab code examples.

resources.name: JOS
resources.desc: Julius Smith's site and his four books are an amazing resource. Matlab/Octave and FAUST code examples included.

resources.name: DAFX Conference Archive
resources.desc: All the papers from the DAFX conference are available online. Another great resource.

resources.name: EarLevel Engineering
resources.desc: Nigel Redmond's DSP blog contains some very nicely written explanations of a variety of topics.

resources.name: Michael Tyson blog
resources.desc: In depth article about Four common mistakes in audio development

resources.name: Ross Bencina's blog/site
resources.desc: A developer who writes a lot of interesting software and articles about lock free programming

resources.name: Sound on Sound Magazine Synth Secrets
resources.desc: A nice series on synthesis techniques.

resources.name: Jatin Chowdhury @ medium
resources.desc: This blog, along with Jatin's github is full of fascinating, cutting-edge stuff.

resources.name: RS-MET tutorials
resources.desc: Some nice pdfs with clear explanations of audio DSP topics.

resources.name: Melatonin Blog
resources.desc: Sudara is writing some really excellent articles on some of the painful tasks involved in audio plug-in development and also publishing lots of useful open source recipes on his github

resources.name: Katja's Home
resources.desc: a very cool site with writings about various DSP topics and examples in pd/c

resources.name: https://audiodev.blog
resources.desc: Matthijs Holleman's blog with some great technical articles and deep dives into resurrecting long lost VST's many of which I used when they first came out!

resources.name: VSCode & Github Codespaces
resources.desc: VSCode is a brilliant text editor that has lots of interesting extensions and functionality. Lately I am using VSCode remote containers and Github Codespaces see video which I think is a game-changing technology.

resources.name: Cycling '74 Max
resources.desc: Max is a great environment to use for prototyping audio plug-ins. There are just so many options for integrating different technologies, I highly recommend it - even if nowadays most of the max patches I make only include a few objects.

resources.name: Desmos
resources.desc: This is an awesome online graphing calculator. Check out some interactive Casio CZ waveforms that I made saw square reso1

resources.name: Coliru
resources.desc: This is an online interactive C++ compiler, which can be a very nice and quick way to test out a particular feature of the language, without having to build a binary.

resources.name: Compiler Explorer
resources.desc: Compiler explorer is a great tool for checking the assembly code that different compilers will produce.

resources.name: FAUST Web IDE
resources.desc: This is an online FAUST IDE and compiler, that lets you test FAUST code with webaudio. You can then tell it to output a zip file with a binary for your preferred platform. This saves you all the trouble of installing FAUST and its dependencies on your local machine.

resources.name: Matplotlib-cpp
resources.desc: A C++ interface to the matplotlib python plotting tool. Allows you to visualize algorithms using the same code that you can use in production.

resources.name: xeus-cling
resources.desc: This is a really cool project allowing you to use JIT compiled C++ in jupyter notebooks - which, like Matplotlib-cpp above is great for visualizing algorithms using the same code that you can use in production, inside the popular jupyter notebook format. Here is an example of how you can use those things together, easily via a ready made docker image.

resources.name: StudioRack plugin manager
resources.desc: Open-source audio plugin manager tool and Github plugin templates to automatically build cross-platform audio plugins.

resources.name: dspplot
resources.desc: A python script that I find useful for plotting filter responses

resources.name: Docker desktop
resources.desc: Docker is incredibly useful for creating reproducible environments, e.g. with specific python libraries installed.

resources.name: Audio Programming Environment - APE
resources.desc: An audio plug-in that embeds a C++ JIT compiler which you can use to test your C++ DSP without leaving the DAW.

resources.name: OhMyZSH
resources.desc: Make macOS terminal/iTerm2 nice and colorful

resources.name: surge
resources.desc: Surge was an excellent product which has been open sourced and is now being maintained and continually improved by the surge-synth team, with a new JUCE UI.
resources.section: Exemplary open source audio plug-in projects

resources.name: valentine
resources.desc: An awesome compressor and great, complete project example for a cross platform audio plug-in in 2023.
resources.section: Exemplary open source audio plug-in projects

resources.name: vital
resources.desc: Vital is a very succesful wavetable synth with a slick interface done using the GPU. Amazing that a project like this can be open source!
resources.section: Exemplary open source audio plug-in projects

resources.name: ni-media
resources.desc: A very nice audio file loading library from Native Instruments

resources.name: choc
resources.desc: From the creator of JUCE comes CHOC, an ISC licensed library of Classy Header-Only Classes. Including some useful audio related utilities

resources.name: BespokeSynth
resources.desc: A pretty amazing modular synth/composition environment with nice real-time visualisation, loads of modules, and lots of flexibility

resources.name: destroyfx
resources.desc: A brilliant collection of open source plug-ins that are very original have been around since the dawn of VST.

resources.name: puredata
resources.desc: Pd is a really nice cross platform dataflow programming environment. Also check out libpd, which you can use as an embeddable DSP runtime in your C++ audio plug-in etc. Camomille combines libpd with JUCE to let you make plug-ins based on Pd patches. plugdata is an excellent new effort to make PD run as a plug-in with a fresh new UI built with JUCE.

resources.name: supercollider
resources.desc: Likewise, but make sure you look at the scsynth part for DSP stuff.

resources.name: csound
resources.desc: CSound is still going strong after many years. It can also be used as an embeddable DSP library. There is a Web IDE, which is a great way to play with interesting scores/orchestras/UDOs that you find on the web and Cabbage lets you make plug-ins based on CSound orchestras.

resources.name: vcvrack
resources.desc: Whilst the other items in this list have been around a while and have somewhat arcane code-bases, this is pretty new and the API is very clean and simple. I think making a VCVRack module it is a great way to get into audio programming.

resources.name: tracktion engine
resources.desc: Source code for an entire DAW engine, using modern C++. An amazing resource for learning all sorts of things including how to structure and architect large audio projects. GPL/Commercial license.

resources.name: musicdsp.org
resources.desc: "A collection of algorithms, thoughts and snippets, gathered for the music dsp community". A long serving site that has recently been revamped. Beware: most of the code there was written a very long time ago, and optimization tricks etc, may not be relevant on modern machines. Also there are lots of code snippets programming languages other than C++ (delphi, java, C# etc). Could do with some curation.

resources.name: obxd
resources.desc: OBxd is a great sounding oberheim emulation plug-in, written with JUCE. DiscoDSP have updated it, and it has also been ported to work on the web as a WebAudioModule

resources.name: dexed
resources.desc: Dexed is a JUCE frontend to Raph Levien's "Music Synthesier For Android", which is an excellent DX7 emulation. Also ported to work on the web as a WebAudioModule

resources.name: AudioKit SynthOne
resources.desc: SynthOne is a great open source project built using Audiokit, that will be very interesting to anyone looking to build an iOS synthesiser.

resources.name: AirWindows Plugins
resources.desc: A large collection of GUI-less plug-ins open source but supported via patreon see airwindows site

resources.name: zita stuff
resources.desc: Fons Adriaensen's linux audio projects offer a lot of great tools for acoustic measurements, spatial audio etc - mostly as jack apps.

resources.name: Webkit's Web Audio API
resources.desc: This is the C++ code for WebKit's implementation of the Web Audio API, as used in Safari.

resources.name: Blink's Web Audio API
resources.desc: The same thing in Blink (Google chromium).

resources.name: Firefox's Web Audio API
resources.desc: And for Mozilla Firefox.

resources.name: GuitarML
resources.desc: Very cool project building open source guitar fx/amp simulations using machine learning techniques.

resources.name: NeuralAmpModeler
resources.desc: A similar project, which is also very cool - plug-in built with iPlug2!

resources.name: ONNXRuntime
resources.desc: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime is a ML inference engine that is well documented, performant, and customizable. Here is an iPlug2 example that I prepared that integrates onnxruntime into an audio plugin, using ort-builder - another project that I made in order to build custom, slimmed down static libraries for the onnxruntime

resources.name: RTNeural
resources.desc: A library designed for realtime inference of Neural Network models with audio in mind. Very small when compared to linking a library like OnnxRuntime or libtensorflow.

resources.name: Torsion Audio's Neural Network Inference Template for Real-Time Cricital Audio Environments
resources.desc: A great JUCE template for a machine learning based plug-in, set up for libTorch, TFLite, or OnnxRuntime, including code to help you offload inference onto a separate thread.

resources.name: KnobMan, WebKnobMan
resources.desc: "Safe for work" knob pics and an online tool to generate them.

resources.name: the owl pedal/module
resources.desc: This is a programmable stomp box and eurorack module that I've been working with since the kick starter campaign to launch it. It's a really nice little unit, which you can program in C++, FAUST, Pd or with Max gen~. I find the limited interface with 4 controls makes me think quite carefully about what's important about my DSP algorithm. You can find some patches I made for it (using a mixture of c++ and FAUST) in the user library, and the original code here.

resources.name: bela
resources.desc: Bela is a wonderful little SoC + Audio Interface which is pretty revolutionary, allowing super low latency audio and sensor I/O all clocked together, in a tiny package. I wrote the FAUST support class for bela. You can also program it with C++ or libpd, and even supercollider.

resources.name: mutable instruments
resources.desc: Emilie Gillet's work is inspirational. The code has been ported to VCVRack and to some nice iOS AUv3s

resources.name: pedalvite
resources.desc: An open source pedal board project from a developer who did a lot of the DSP in the best plugins of the last ~20 years.

resources.name: Daisy
resources.desc: Daisy is a brilliant programmable embedded music platform. A few different host devices are available into which you plug the "daisy seed" Of course you can also build your own device around the Daisy seed board if you don't suck at electronics, like me. It has a more powerful MCU than the OWL and I really like how the same board can be plugged into different hardware depending on your needs.

resources.name: Jan Wilczek - The WolfSound
resources.desc: Jan is an extremely driven, friendly and talented guy who has put a lot of work into making a great set of resources for people who want to learn audio programming. His content is a mixture of very good technical overviews of important topics and great interviews with people across the industry and involved in academia. I was honoured to be interviewed by Jan for episode 15 of the wolfsound podcast, which you can listen to here.

resources.name: TheAudioProgrammer
resources.desc: includes a lot of tutorials about JUCE with guest slots on things like web audio.

resources.name: TheChernoProject
resources.desc: although this channel is focused on game development, the C++ series is excellent. Highly recommended.

resources.name: Valerio Verlardo - The Sound of AI
resources.desc: Valerio has made a very impressive channel and community dedicated to AI and ML topics in Audio

resources.name: ToteBagLabs - Lofi Audio Effects Prototyping to chill/relax to
resources.desc: My friend and Ableton colleague Jose is recording his work developing plug-ins in Juce/C++ and DSP code using CMajor.

resources.name: Teaching Yourself to Make Music Software: Steve Duda in Conversation | Loop
resources.desc: an inspiring interview with a great developer about a killer synth.

resources.name: Sean Costello (Valhalla DSP) on reverb design
resources.desc: great talk by another great plugin developer

resources.name: C++ Real-Time Audio Programming with Bela
resources.desc: a very clearly presented course.

resources.name: Vadim Zavalishin - The Art of VA Filter Design, ADC 2018
How Moog Makes Synth Apps: Interview With Geert Bevin, Head Of Software At Moog
resources.desc: a great interview full of insight

resources.name: musicdsp mailing list
resources.desc: The music DSP mailing list is pretty quiet these days, but it still worth signing up, despite the web 0-1 front page. Every now and again a music DSP legend posts something interesting.

resources.name: KvR Audio DSP and Plug-in Development Forum
resources.desc: This is probably the most active forum for audio DSP that is not aligned with a particular plug-in framework. There are some very smart people, some mavericks and some plain weirdos who hang out here.

resources.name: JUCE Forums
resources.desc: This is a collection of forums centred around the variety of things that JUCE does. Since there are such a huge amount of people using JUCE to make audio software, there is a lot of good info here.

resources.name: Cockos Forums
resources.desc: Another collection of forums centred around Cockos' tools including one for WDL/iPlug and one for Reaper JS.

resources.name: The audio developer conference (ADC)
resources.desc: Whilst the other places mentioned here are all virtual, this is a real conference where you can go and meet real people face-to-face who do audio programming - highly recommended!

resources.name: TheAudioProgrammer Discord server
resources.desc: A popular community for discussing audio programming.

resources.name: iPlug2 Forum
resources.desc: forum for iPlug2 discussions

resources.name: Steinberg VST3 Forum
resources.desc: A forum for the VST3 SDK/format
